tagline: Up Topanga Creek from the sea into the Santa Monica Mountains.
intro: A mile up from the Pacific Coast Highway, Topanga Canyon Boulevard leaves the beach behind and follows Topanga Creek up the canyon into the Santa Monica Mountains. The scenic stretch is only two and a half miles long, where the road cuts through Topanga State Park. In the 1920s this was a weekend getaway, with summer cabins along the creek.

The road has its hazards. In January 2005 a 300-ton boulder rolled down a hillside onto the boulevard and shut it for about a week, and the first try with dynamite failed because the rock was soaked through with rain.

moments.title: Topanga Creek
moments.text: The creek beside the road is one of the few undammed waterways left in the area, and a spawning ground for steelhead trout.

moments.title: Topanga
moments.text: Up the canyon the blacklisted actor Will Geer settled his family in the 1950s, with Woody Guthrie in a shack on the plot, and an artists' colony grew up unintended.
